legend: A) Malignant single cells, small epithelial clusters and even small glands extensively involve all layers of the epidermis of the nipple. The underlying dermis shows a prominent lymphocytic infiltrate.
The neoplastic epithelium consists of large cells with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli.
The tumour cells appear pigmented, but they were negative for melanocytic markers and expressed CK7, consistent with MPD.
Small clusters and single cells with high-grade nuclei and prominent nucleoli are present in the basal layers of the epidermis of the nipple.
HER2 protein is expressed in the cell membrane in mammary Paget disease. (HER2 immunohistochemical stain)
The cells are scattered singly or in clusters.
Tumour cells with copious pale cytoplasm and conspicuous nucleoli infiltrating the intraepidermal layer.
Immunostaining of CK7 demonstrates positive expression within the tumour cells.
There is infiltration of the epidermis by single cells with pleomorphic nulcei and associated lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates of the underlying dermis.
The neoplastic cells show HER-2 positivity

Nipple shows focal surface erosion and a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the upper dermis. The epidermis contains individual and clusters of high grade malignant cells indicative of Paget disease. Occasional small clusters of abnormal epithelial cells are found in the superficial stroma, detached from the epidermis, suggesting focal microinvasion.

diagnosis: Mammary Paget Disease with a minute cluster highly suspicious for superficial microinvasion
legend: Large cells with marked nuclear atypia and prominent nucleoli form conspicuous clusters in the basal layer of the epidermis and are present as smaller clusters or single cells in the more superficial layers. The epidermis shows hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, but is not ulcerated. A minute cluster consisting of two-three malignant epithelial cells in the superficial dermis in a focus of dense lymphocytic infiltrate is highly suspicious for microinvasive carcinoma (hematoxylin eosin stain).
